items.text: After 66 years of being in place, the Constitutional Court of Korea ruled that South Korea’s anti-abortion law was unconstitutional. It said that the law is ‘an unconstitutional restriction that violates a pregnant woman’s right to choose’. The court reviewed the law after a doctor challenged the ban, as he had been convicted of performing nearly 70 abortions from 2013 to 2015. Exceptions to the law have only been in life- threatening pregnancies, rape or incest. Doctors who perform abortions can face prison for up to two years, and the women get a fine of more than $1,700 and a year in prison, too. The ruling is making way for South Korea to make abortions legal, although the parliament now has until the end of 2020 to revise the law. Difficult words: violate (break), exception (a special case), -threatening (putting in danger). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In South Korea, there is a law which bans abortions . People first put it into place 66 years ago. Abortions are legal in the country only for some situations such as if she is in danger of real life, or if someone raped her. The Constitutional Court of Korea looked into the law, and it says that it is against the constitution that abortions are illegal. The court says that a pregnant woman must have the right to choose. The Korean parliament now must change the law by the end of 2020. Difficult words: ban (make illegal), abortion (stopping pregnancy – ‘killing’ a baby inside a woman’s body), rape (force a woman to have sex when she does not want to). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a law in South Korea. It is a 66-year-old law. It makes abortions illegal . They are legal only in special cases. The Constitutional Court of Korea looks into the law. It says that this law is against the constitution. The law must change. The Korean parliament must change it by the end of 2020. Difficult words: abortion (stopping a pregnancy – ‘killing’ a baby inside a woman’s body), illegal (people must not do illegal things, but they can do legal things), constitutional (about the constitution – the most important law), court (an institution where lawyers work; they say if something is legal or illegal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to the country’s government, homelessness in France increased from approximately 93,000 in 2001 to more than 141,000 in 2012. A French charity also says that at least one person dies every day there as a result of living on the street. Recently, people criticised the French government for not doing enough to act on the homelessness crisis. The United Nations’ special rapporteur said that there is not enough affordable housing, including social housing for the people who need it. She also said, ‘ evictions into homelessness are strictly prohibited under international law’. She said that France could improve its housing laws, find houses for the poor and stop all forced evictions. Difficult words: rapporteur (a person who gives reports on something), affordable (less expensive), eviction (throwing someone out from their home). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Homelessness in France is getting worse. In 2001, there were around 93,000 homeless people, and in 2012, there were more than 141,000. A French charity also says that at least one person dies every day there because he or she is homeless. The United Nations says that the French government is not doing enough to lower the homelessness. The organisation says that there is not enough affordable housing and social housing . Forced evictions are also a problem. Difficult words: affordable housing (homes which are less expensive), social housing (homes for very poor people), forced evictions (throwing someone on the street). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2001, 93,000 people in France live on the streets. In 2012, 141,000 people live on the streets. More and more people in France do not have homes. The situation is getting worse. One person dies every day there because they do not have a home. The United Nations looks at the situation in France. The UN says that the French government is not working to lower the homelessness . The UN says that France must do something about this problem. Difficult words: government (the ‘bosses/leaders’ of a country), lower (make less/smaller), homelessness (the situation when somebody is homeless – has no home). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A bomb went off in a market in western Pakistan last Friday, killing at least 20 and injuring many more. The country’s prime minister called the bombing a terrorist attack and condemned it. The bombing took place in the city of Quetta. Among the dead are at least seven Hazaras and one paramilitary soldier – the city is home to a large community of Hazaras, a Shia Muslim minority. According to CNN, a Sunni militant group claimed responsibility for the bombing. Quetta’s police chief said that security forces escort members of the Hazaras community to the market each day and that paramilitary soldiers and police were patrolling the area when the bomb exploded. The Pakistani prime minister called for additional security in the city. Difficult words: condemn (say that something is terrible), escort (come with to protect), patrol (watch to make safe). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A bomb exploded in a market in western Pakistan last Friday. At least 20 people died and many more were injured. A large community of Hazaras live in the city where the bombing took place. Hazaras are a Shia Muslim minority . Soldiers and police escort them to the market each day, and there were guards when the bomb exploded. At least seven Hazaras and one soldier died in the attack. According to CNN, a Sunni militant group claimed responsibility for the bombing. Difficult words: minority (a group of people who are somehow different from most people in a place; usually, some people do not like some minorities), escort (come with to protect), claim responsibility (say that you did something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Hazaras people live in one city in Pakistan. They are a minority . They are Shia Muslims. Police and soldiers go with them when they go somewhere in the city. They protect them. Last Friday, a bomb explodes in the city. Twenty people die. Many people are injured. Seven Hazaras and one soldier die in the attack. CNN says that a Sunni militant group says that it does the attack. Difficult words: minority (a group of people who are somehow different from most people; usually, some people do not like some minorities), Shia and Sunni (two types of Islam), militant group (a group of people who want to change something by fighting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The USA designated Iran’s army as a foreign terrorist organisation last Monday. This was the first time that America had given such a name to another country’s military. Trump said that the action sends a clear message to Tehran that its support for terrorism has serious consequences . The US government had been thinking of doing this for years. In 2007, it did so for an Iranian military group which operates internationally. Before the American government officially gave the news, Iranian lawmakers called it ‘ inappropriate and idiotic’ and promised to react. Difficult words: designate (officially give a name/label/status), consequence (effect), inappropriate (not appropriate – suitable, right). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Monday, the USA officially called Iran’s army a foreign terrorist organisation. This is the first time that America called another country’s army ‘terrorists’. Trump said this sends Iran a message that its support for terrorism has serious effects. The American government was thinking of doing this for years. In 2007, it called a part of the Iranian army terrorists. This group operates internationally. Before the American government officially gave the news, Iranians said that this was ‘ inappropriate and idiotic’. They also promised to react. Difficult words: support (help), government (the people who are the bosses/leaders of a country), inappropriate (not appropriate – suitable, right). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about Iran and the USA. The USA says that the Iranian army is a terrorist organisation. This is the first time that the USA calls a country’s army ‘terrorists’. Trump says that this sends Iran a strong message. Iran says that this is ‘ inappropriate and idiotic ’. Iran says that it will react to this. Difficult words: inappropriate (not right), idiotic (stupid), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Australian parliament approved controversial new legislation on April 4th. This new law means that tech executives could go to prison if they take too long to remove violent content from their websites. The type of content includes terrorism, murder, attempted murder, torture, rape and kidnapping. Penalties include up to three years in jail for the executives and a fine of 7.5 million dollars for the company or more. The aim of the law is to make sure that people cannot spread violent and extreme propaganda online. The lawyers say that the Internet should not be used as a weapon for evil. The new law is a reaction to the deadly Christchurch mosque shootings last month in which 50 people died. The shooter spread violent video of the killings across social media. Difficult words: approve (say ‘yes’ to something), controversial (some people like it and some people do not), executive (a manager in a position of power). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last month, there was a shooting in New Zealand when fifty people died. The killer shared the video of the murder online. The Australian parliament thinks that the Internet should not be a place for sharing videos like this. It passes a new law that says that social media companies must take the content down. If they take too long, they can pay 7.5 million dollars or more. Some of their employees can go to prison for up to three years. The type of illegal content is terrorism, killing somebody or trying to kill them, torture and more. There is a lot of debate around the new law. Some people are for it, and some people are against it. Difficult words: pass (say ‘yes’), content (things like pictures and videos), torture (the act of torturing somebody – making them feel a lot of pain). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last month, there is a terrorist attack in New Zealand. A man shoots at people. Fifty people die. He films the situation. Everyone can see it on the Internet. The Australian parliament does not like this. It thinks that videos like this must not be on the Internet. It says ‘yes’ to a new law . This law says that companies like Facebook or Twitter must take down videos like this. If the companies do not, they must pay money. This can be 7.5 million dollars or more. The people who work at the Internet company can even go to prison. Difficult words: parliament (a government), law (an official document which say what somebody can and must not do), take down (stop). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US Food and Drug Administration is looking into 35 reports of people having seizures after they used e-cigarettes from 2010–2019. Thirty-five reports is a small number, but an important enough number that the administration wants to look into it. The administration would like people who had these issues to report them on its website. Young people are in many of the reports, but there are no other obvious patterns. It is unclear if there is a direct link between seizures and vaping , although seizures can come from nicotine poisoning. The administration will also look into other risks of e-cigarettes. Last month, other federal regulators wanted more rules for selling flavoured e-cigarettes because teenagers are using them so much. Difficult words: vape (smoke an e-cigarette; slang for vapour), nicotine (an addictive chemical in cigarettes and in some e-cigarettes), regulator (a rule maker). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A US government organisation is looking into 35 reports about e-cigarettes from 2010–2019. In the reports, people have seizures after they use e-cigarettes. Thirty-five reports is a small number but an important number. The organisation wants to know more. It asks people to report these problems on its website. Young people are in many of the reports. It is not clear that vaping causes seizures, but seizures can come from nicotine poisoning. The administration wants to look into other problems with e-cigarettes. Difficult words: seizure (when your brain suddenly stops working correctly because of the electricity in the brain changes), vape (smoke an e-cigarette – an electronic cigarette), nicotine (a chemical inside of cigarettes and in some e-cigarettes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An American government organisation has 35 reports from 2010–2019. These reports show that people have seizures after they use e-cigarettes. The organisation is worried. It wants to know more. It asks people to give more information. They can put the problems on its website. Young people are in many of the reports. It is not obvious if vaping makes the seizures happen. However, cigarettes or e-cigarettes can make seizures happen. They have nicotine in them which can cause seizures. Nicotine is a chemical. Difficult words: government (the group of people who are the leaders/bosses of a country), seizure (when your brain suddenly stops working correctly), vape (smoke an e-cigarette). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

When President Obama was in office in the USA, he made stronger rules for federal nutritional standards for salt and whole grains in school meals. Last Wednesday, multiple states sued the Trump administration for weakening those rules. They are suing the US Department of Agriculture , the Food and Nutrition Service, and Secretary Sonny Perdue. Previous First Lady Michelle Obama helped create those rules and she criticised the change. She asked why the government does not want children to have healthy food at school. Difficult words: nutritional (about food), whole grains (for example, whole grain bread is healthier than white bread), agriculture (relating to farms and growing and distributing food). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

When President Obama was president of the USA, he made stronger rules on what types of food children can get at school. Last Wednesday, some states sued organisations in the Trump administration because they made those rules weaker. Michelle Obama was President Obama’s First Lady. She helped create the stronger rules and she criticised the change. She asked why the government does not want children to have good food at school. Difficult words: sue (go to court and say that somebody is doing something bad), administration (the people who are Trump’s government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

President Trump is the president of the USA. President Obama was the president before him. When Obama is president, he makes stronger food rules for schools. He wants the food to be healthy. Trump’s administration has different ideas. People change these food rules. The school food does not have to be as healthy. Last Wednesday, some states sue the Trump administration. Michelle Obama is President Obama’s First Lady. She helps make the stronger rules. She asks why the government makes the changes. She asks why the government does not want children to have good food at school. Difficult words: was (past of ‘is’), rule (something which tells you what you can and must not do), administration (the people who work for Trump), s ue (to go to court and say that somebody is doing something bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There have been more than 3,000 complaints about certain Kia and Hyundai models for risk of catching fire, including claims of 103 injuries and one death in the USA. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) announced investigations into certain years of the Hyundai Sonata and Santa Fe, and Kia Optima, Sorento and Soul models. There could be up to 3 million Hyundai and Kia vehicles at an increased risk of catching fire. Difficult words: complaint (when somebody complains about something – says that there is something wrong with it), claim (saying something which is not clear if it is true), announce (officially say something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More than 3,000 people complained about some Kia and Hyundai cars. The problem was that some of the cars catch on fire. Since there were so many cases , an American agency started an investigation into this problem. Some years of the Hyundai Sonata and Santa Fe, and Kia Optima, Sorento and Soul have a higher risk of catching on fire. There can be up to 3 million of these cars on the road in the USA. Difficult words: complain (say that there is something wrong with something), case (a situation with a bad car), agency (a government institution). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about cars. Some Kia and Hyundai cars are bad. Some of them catch on fire. This happens to about 3,000 people. The people tell an American agency about this. The agency starts an investigation . The problems are with Hyundai Sonata and Santa Fe, and Kia Optima, Sorento and Soul. There can be up to 3 million of these cars on the road in the USA. Difficult words: agency (an organisation which works for the people of a country), investigation (a type of work to get more information about a problem and to understand it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Upwards of 40,000 people gathered on Saturday March 31st along the Israel–Gaza border to mark the anniversary of the Great March of Return protest. Palestinians have been protesting at the border every week for the past year, demanding the right to return to the ancestral land that they say they lost when Israel was created. Palestinian officials say that Israeli police killed more than 250 Palestinians since the protests began in March 2018. The protesters also demand the nullification of the Israeli blockade – a combination of air, sea and land travel restrictions which isolate the area from resources. Difficult words: gather (come together in large numbers), ancestral (something a people had for many generations), nullification (cancel, stop). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More than 40,000 people protested along the Israel–Gaza border on Saturday March 31st. They marked the anniversary of the Great March of Return protest. Since March 2018, there were protests at the border every week. The Palestinians demand their land which they say Israel took from them. In the year of protests, the Israeli police killed more than 250 Palestinians. Difficult words: mark (remember), anniversary (the date when something happened a year/years ago), demand (want, ask for). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Gaza. In March 2018, Palestinians start to protest. They call the protest the Great March of Return. Palestinians protest every week. They want their land back. They say that Israel has taken their land. One year later, there is a big protest. Forty thousand people protest in March 2019. In one year of the protests, Israeli police kill 250 Palestinians. Difficult words: has taken (present perfect of ‘take’; it happened already and it is done). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Korea declared a national emergency after massive wildfires spread across the country. Thousands of people evacuated, fires destroyed more than 100 homes, fires injured eleven people, and at least two people have died. The BBC reported that a spark from a transformer in a city northeast of Seoul probably started the fire last Thursday. The fire then quickly spread from strong winds – it burned more than 1,300 acres of land. The military joined the firefighters to battle the flames. They contained one fire, but half-contained a second one by Friday. Difficult words: spark (a small piece of fire or ‘electricity’ which can start a large fire), transformer (a machine for changing one type of electricity to another), contain (bring under control). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There are big wildfires in South Korea. Thousands of people evacuate, fires destroy more than 100 homes, they injure eleven people, and at least two people died. People say that it is possible that a spark from a transformer started the fire last Thursday. Due to strong winds, the fire grew quickly. By Friday, it had burned more than 1,300 acres of land. Difficult words: wildfire (a large fire which burns trees, bushes and grass), spark (a small piece of fire or ‘electricity’ which can start a big fire), transformer (a machine for changing one type of electricity to another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There are big wildfires in South Korea. Thousands of people evacuate . Fires destroy more than 100 homes. They injure eleven people. Two or more people die. One big fire started last Thursday. In one day, it burns 1,300 acres of land. Difficult words: wildfire (a large fire which burns trees, bushes and grass), evacuate (move away from danger), started (past of ‘start’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The American health organisation CDC (the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) reported that the number of confirmed measles cases in the USA so far this year is higher than for all of 2018. Measles is a respiratory illness that is highly contagious but vaccine-preventable. Health regulators recommend the children be immunised against 14 preventable diseases by the time that they are six years old. The CDC says that there are six outbreaks in the USA – that includes the state of New York where a state of emergency was declared. In Rockland County, unvaccinated children were also banned from public spaces. If states do not enact stricter vaccination rules, the federal government might step in with nation-wide measures. Difficult words: confirm (prove, say/show that something is true), respiratory (affecting the organs of respiration – the organs that people breathe with), contagious (able to spread from one person to another). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

From January to end of March, there were more cases of measles in the USA than in the whole year of 2018. Measles is an illness which affects the respiratory organs (the organs for breathing). It can spread easily from person to person, but vaccination can prevent it. There are six places in the USA where measles is a big problem. One of them is the state of New York. In one of its areas, unvaccinated children must not be in public spaces. Difficult words: case (a situation when somebody has measles), spread (go, jump), vaccination (giving people an injection so that they will not get ill), prevent (to stop something bad from happening in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about measles. Measles is an illness . It attacks the organs for breathing . In the USA, people have problems with the measles. There are many cases of measles. From January to March of 2019, there are more cases of measles than in all of 2018. The situation is bad. American leaders are trying to do something about it. Difficult words: illness (viruses or bacteria which attack the body and make you sick or even kill you), breathe (take air into the body), case (a situation when somebody has measles). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Tuesday, the state-run Algerian press agency announced in a statement that the country’s ailing president, Abdelaziz Bouteflika, resigned following weeks of protests. This comes as a surprise since the president previously announced plans to run for a fifth term. However, people started protesting him as soon as they found out. Bouteflika first came to power in 1999 when the military largely backed his victory. This led to criticism that he won the presidency fraudulently . People elected him again in 2004, 2009 and 2014, and the criticism never stopped. The 82-year-old president has been in poor health recently – he survived a stroke in 2013. Difficult words: announce (officially say something), ailing (in poor health), fraudulently (done illegally). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Abdelaziz Bouteflika is the Algerian president who first came to power in 1999. The military backed his victory and people criticised him for that. Some people said that he did not win legally. People elected him again in 2004, 2009 and 2014. The criticism never stopped, and people protested when he said that he was going to run for the fifth term . Most recently, however, the president resigned, as he is 82 years old and ill. Difficult words: back (support, help), elect (choose a leader), term (the time when somebody is president). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Abdelaziz Bouteflika is the Algerian president. He first becomes president in 1999. People elect him again in 2004, 2009 and 2014. Some people elect him. Some people do not. Some people criticise him. They say that he becomes president illegally . In 2019, he is still president. He wants to be president for more five years. He tells this to people. They start to protest. Most recently , he stops being president. He tells this to people. He is ill. He is 82 years old. Difficult words: elect (choose a leader), illegally (not legally – criminally), most recently (a little while ago). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The company Monsanto makes a herbicide called Roundup that is popular because it works so well at killing weeds around the plants that you want to grow. A chemical in the herbicide is glyphosate, and a jury found that the ingredient caused a man from California to develop cancer. However, there is disagreement on what glyphosate does to people. The World Health Organisation said that it could damage a person’s DNA . Bayer, the parent company of Monsanto, said that this is untrue and it would change its products if they were unsafe. In the US, there are 11,000 cases against Bayer due to effects from its herbicides. Difficult words: herbicide (a chemical that kills plants), DNA (the carrier of genetic information), due to (because of). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Monsanto is a company which sells a popular herbicide called Roundup. Roundup kills weeds around the plants that you want to grow. A court said that an ingredient in the herbicide made a man get cancer. People are not sure what the ingredient does to people. The World Health Organisation said that it could hurt people. Bayer, the parent company of Monsanto, said that this is not true. It said that if its products are not safe, it will change them. In the USA, there are 11,000 cases against Bayer because of problems from its herbicides. Difficult words: herbicide (a product that kills plants), weed (a plant that you do not want to grow but it grows with your plants anyway), case (when you get a lawyer and officially say that something is illegal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Monsanto is a company. It makes Roundup. Roundup kills weeds. It works well. It is very popular. A court says that the Roundup gives a man cancer. People are not sure what Roundup does to people. Many people think that it is not safe. Bayer is a big company. It owns Monsanto. It says that Roundup is safe. However, there are 11,000 cases against Bayer in the USA. Difficult words: weed (a plant which you do not want), court (an institution which says if somebody does or does not do something wrong), case (when you get a lawyer and officially say that something bad is happening). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People are unhappy with how Twitter and other social media companies do nothing when famous people post hate speech online. Twitter is trying to figure how to flag those tweets instead of deleting them so that people will still know about them. Twitter might use an annotation with an explanation to show that the tweet did not follow Twitter’s rules. Facebook says that it will ban hate speech from white supremacists early this month. Difficult words: flag (to show that there is something not OK about the tweets), annotation (a comment), white supremacist (a person who thinks that white people are better than non-white people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People say that Twitter and other social media do nothing when famous people say something hateful online. Twitter wants to flag hate speech instead of deleting it, and it is thinking how to do this. For example, Twitter can comment on the Tweet. The commentary would explain how the Tweet does not follow Twitter’s rules. Facebook says that it will ban hate speech from white supremacists early this month. Difficult words: flag (show that there is something not OK about the tweets), ban (stop something from happening), white supremacist (a person who thinks that white people are better than non-white people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people are criticising website like Twitter and Facebook. The people do not like that nothing happens when famous people say something hateful on these websites. Twitter plans to flag hateful Tweets. It does not want to delete these Tweets. It wants to put a comment on them. These comments can tell people why the Tweet has a flag. Facebook is changing, too. It wants to stop comments from white supremacists . Facebook wants to do this in this month. Difficult words: hateful (hateful text makes some people feel very bad), flag (show that there is something not OK about the tweets), white supremacist (a person who thinks that white people are better than non-white people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Friday, New York state lawmakers agreed to impose a ban on most kinds of plastic bags from retailers . The ban will go into effect in March of next year. However, you could still get a plastic bag for food take-out, newspapers, clothes, and big plastic trash bags. Right now, California and Hawaii are the only American states with a ban on plastic bags. Difficult words: impose (put), ban (the act of banning something – making it illegal), retailer (a shop or a person who sells something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Lawmakers of the New York state are banning plastics bags. They say that the ban will go into effect of March next year. Plastic bags are going to be banned from retailers , but there will be some exceptions . For example, you will still be able to get a plastic bag for food take-out, newspapers, clothes, and big plastic trash bags. Right now, California and Hawaii are the only American states with a ban on plastic bags. Difficult words: ban (make something illegal), retailer (a shop or a person who sells something), exception (a thing which will not be banned). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US state of New York is banning plastic bags. The ban is going to start next March. However, not all plastic bags are going to be banned. For example, people are going to be able to buy plastic bags for clothes, newspapers, and take-out food. Right now, in the USA, there are only two states with a ban on plastic bags. They are California and Hawaii. Difficult words: ban (make something illegal), is/are going to (in the future), be able (can). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Parliament voted 410 to 192 in favour of scrapping the summer time by 2021. The next step involves discussing the issues with members of the bloc . Under current EU law, member countries move their clocks forward together on the last Sunday in March and all of them move back on the last Sunday in October. The use of the summer time is often said to save energy, but the European commission says that those savings are small. On top of that, an EU-wide survey from last year showed that most people are in favour of stopping the clock change. Difficult words: in favour (for, not against), scrap (cancel, stop), bloc (an alliance, a large group). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The European Parliament voted for cancelling the summer time by 2021. The next step is to discuss the issue with EU countries. The current law makes EU countries move their clocks forward on the last Sunday in March and move them backwards on the last Sunday in October. Some people say that the summer time saves energy, but the European commission says that the savings are small. Also, most people in the EU want to cancel the summer time. Difficult words: cancel (stop), issue (a topic or problem for discussion), current (existing now). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Europe, people have summer time. In March, they move their clocks forward. In October, they move them back. Some people say that the summer time saves energy. The European commission says that the savings are small. The European Parliament takes a vote . It votes to cancel the summer time by 2021. EU countries now can talk about it. Difficult words: European commission (an important organisation of the EU), take a vote (vote – say if you want or do not want something to happen), cancel (stop). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Wednesday, the first five cases of cholera in Mozambique were confirmed. As of Friday, that number rose to 139. In the city of Beira, the risk of a cholera outbreak is very high. This disease causes diarrhoea , and it can be deadly if the ill person is not helped. People typically contract it from infected water or food. The World Health Organisation sent over 900 cholera vaccines and 21 medical teams to the affected African country. Difficult words: outbreak (epidemic, when many people have it), diarrhoea (when you have to poop very often and the poop is like water; this disease can kill you because it makes you lose the water in your body), contract (catch). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Cholera is a disease which causes diarrhoea . If ill people do not get help, it can kill them. Last Wednesday, five people had cholera in Mozambique. On Friday, 139 people had it. There is a risk that more people will catch it. People can catch this disease from water or food. The World Health Organisation is trying to help. It sent 900 cholera vaccines and 21 medical teams to Mozambique. Difficult words: disease (a thing/virus/bacteria which makes you ill), diarrhoea (when you have to poop very often and the poop is like water; this sickness can kill you because you have no water in your body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Cholera is a disease . It is very dangerous. If ill people do not get help, they can die. Mozambique is a country in Africa. Last Wednesday, five people have cholera there. On Friday, 139 people have it. This is bad. More and more people can catch it. The World Health Organisation is trying to help. It sends 21 teams of doctors to Mozambique. Difficult words: disease (a thing/viruses/bacteria which makes you ill). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Wednesday, India carried out its first successful anti-satellite missile test. India destroyed the satellite in low-Earth orbit so that the debris would not be left out in space. India’s prime minister announced the news a month ahead of the country’s general elections . Opposition leaders criticised the timing, and they are saying that Narendra Modi used this to gain popularity. Others are also worried about the possibility of weaponising space. Three other countries (the USA, Russia and China) conducted similar tests. One critic is, unsurprisingly, India’s neighbour of Pakistan. The two countries have been fighting over the Kashmir region since the late 1940s. Difficult words: debris (broken pieces of something), announce (officially say something), elections (when the people choose their leaders). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Big Ben is the UK’s most iconic symbol. Since 2017, the Elizabeth Tower and the distinctive sound of Big Ben (the bell inside) have been undergoing renovation . The structure is 160 years old and has needed maintenance work throughout its lifetime. For many years, people always painted the hands and numbers of the clock black, but last Thursday, the workers revealed the clock’s original colour of Prussian blue. The new surfaces are made from stones, silver, gold and glass. The renovation work, which will continue until 2021, will also redo the roof and see that the stone inside is protected from water. The work is far from finished, but this week gave people an idea of what the tower will look like when all is finished. Difficult words: distinctive (typical), renovation (the work to make something old work well again), maintenance work (work to keep something working well). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Moscow, a 5-year-old girl lived in squalor in an apartment due to her mother’s neglect . The girl lived with trash all around her, the furniture was smashed, and dirt covered the walls. There was no water and electricity as the mother had not paid the bills. The girl is now in hospital. A spokesperson for children’s rights said that the girl would not eat the food that people offered her, but she would smell it and hold it. She said that the girl needs to learn how to sleep in a bed and is also afraid of water. Another person said that the girl appears to not know how to speak. Police arrested the mother and are investigating the situation. Difficult words: squalor (extreme dirtiness), due to (because of), neglect (when someone does not do the things he or she needs to do to take care of a person, an animal or a place). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
